## Autonomous secrets-rotation attempt — OUTCOME: nothing rotated (all deferred). No AWS mutation performed.

Per operator authorization to rotate ONLY secrets that are (a) mintable by me AND (b) non-breaking/self-healing, with `terraform apply` still forbidden. I enumerated every SecureString from `local.rebar_secret_params` (infra/terraform/ssm.tf) plus the auth `/auth-solutions/COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET`, verified `ssm:PutParameter` is allowed for my identity (`arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier`, us-east-1), and classified each. **After investigation, ZERO secrets qualify as autonomous-rotatable — every candidate has a hard blocker. I ran no `put-parameter` and no `terraform apply`.**

### Classification table

**AUTONOMOUS-ROTATABLE — (none)**
On investigation, the two nominally "random/mintable" candidates both failed the non-breaking/self-healing test (details below). No secret was rotated.

**COORDINATION-SENSITIVE — DEFER (mintable, but rotation breaks a chain this workflow / another consumer depends on)**
| Secret | Why deferred |
|---|---|
| `/auth-solutions/COOKIE_SIGNING_SECRET` (SSO cookie-signing key) | **Named by the task as the autonomous example — but investigation shows it is NOT.** The key is **baked into Lambda@Edge bundles at deploy** (edge functions can't read SSM at runtime). I found **`lmn-sso-gate` + `lmn-staging-sso-gate`** (nodejs20.x, mod 2026-08-12) DEPLOYED, fronting the `modernization-navigator[-staging].solutions.navateam.com` CloudFront distributions (the Legacy-Modernization-Navigator app — a **different team/project** sharing this domain's SSO). Rotating the SSM value → auth-host signs cookies with the NEW key while those baked edge gates verify with the OLD key → **modernization-navigator production SSO breaks** until LMN redeploys its edge bundles. Not self-healing, cross-team, and outside the stated `/rebar/prod/*` scope. The runbook's "rebar currently runs no gate instance" is true only for rebar; LMN's gates are live. Write-only, so no true rollback either. → **DEFER to a coordinated LMN-inclusive window.** |
| `/rebar/prod/opcert-ed25519-key` | Op-cert attestation signing key underpinning plan-review / completion-verifier — the gates THIS close-chain uses. DEFER (task's own default). |
| `/rebar/prod/mcp-hmac-signing-key` | "verdict signing" (fetch-secrets.sh:13) — MCP gate-verdict signing chain. Rotating mid-session risks verdict-signature verification. DEFER. |
| `/rebar/prod/rebar-bot-signing-key` | Authorship/attestation signing; also mirrored to GHA secret `REBAR_BOT_SIGNING_KEY` — must rotate the pair together. DEFER. |
| `/rebar/prod/opcert-origin-guard` | **terraform-GENERATED** (`random_password`), injected as an API-GW header. Can't rotate out-of-band without tf drift + header mismatch (needs an apply). DEFER. |
| `/rebar/prod/gerrit-ssh-host-ed25519-key` | SSH **host** key — rotating trips `known_hosts` for every client incl. CI's SSH-to-Gerrit Verified-vote path. Not self-healing. DEFER. |
| `/rebar/prod/gerrit-admin-password` | Mintable but must also be set on the Gerrit account (external coordination). DEFER. |

**EXTERNAL-MANUAL — DEFER (third-party issued; I cannot mint)**
`github-oauth-client-secret`, `reviewbot-tickets-pat`, `mcp-tickets-pat`, `mcp-client-pat-copilot|claude|codex`, `g2p-github-pat`, `github-*` (replication deploy key), `gerrit-bot-token`, `jira-api-token`, `anthropic-api-key`, and the `alert-endpoint` webhook URL (config value, not mintable). Each requires a human in an external console/provider.

### Nothing rotated — and why that's the safe outcome
The task said "default to defer" for coordination-sensitive secrets and "if a rotation breaks something, stop." My investigation caught the break **before** it happened: the one secret named as the autonomous example (cookie key) would have taken down another team's production SSO. Everything else is external, terraform-managed, or feeds the very gates/session in use. So the correct, evidence-based result is **zero autonomous rotations**.

### Remaining manual steps (all deferred to the operator maintenance window)
1. **The `value_wo` cutover `terraform apply`** (this ticket's step 1) — clobbers all 21 SecureStrings to `CHANGEME`; must be operator-supervised.
2. **Re-seed / rotate ALL 21 real values in the SAME window** (step 2) — since the cutover resets every slot, this is mandatory regardless of any pre-rotation; any value I might have set would just be re-clobbered.
3. **Cross-team coordination for the cookie key**: schedule the LMN edge-gate (`lmn-sso-gate` / `lmn-staging-sso-gate`) redeploy alongside any cookie-secret rotation, or `modernization-navigator` SSO breaks.
4. **External rotations** (step 2 crown-jewels + all EXTERNAL-MANUAL secrets) in each provider console, updating every dependent system (GHA mirrors, Gerrit/Jira accounts, GitHub OAuth app, Anthropic console).
5. **State scrub** (steps 3–4): verify `terraform state pull` shows no SecureString value; purge historical cleartext from the retained `s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate` versions.

No secret values are recorded here or anywhere. `9350` and the rubied ticket remain OPEN (their clean-apply close is gated on this deferred cutover). Change 2389 (config-only import blocks) worktree kept intact.

**Update — Step 1 (the `terraform apply` cutover) is DONE, value-preservingly. Exposure remediation (state-history scrub + rotation) REMAINS the open scope of this ticket.**

Under standing operator authorization, the `value_wo` migration was applied this session as a **structural-only, value-PRESERVING** cutover (tracked via bug `9350-174a-3320-4e33` / `improvised-altophobic-azurevase`, now closed). Rather than the runbook's default "one-time cutover reset" (which sends `value_wo="CHANGEME"` and resets every live prod SecureString to a placeholder), current live values were staged as `value_wo` behind a fail-closed var seam so the forced first send wrote back **byte-identical** values.

Result: `3 imported, 0 added, 20 changed, 0 destroyed`; all 20 managed SecureString values byte-preserved (decrypted sha256 diff, identical for every key); `value_wo_version = 1` on all 20; the 20 managed slots now hold **no cleartext in state**. `terraform plan` on committed config is now clean ("No changes"). No secrets rotated, no external systems touched, no operator involvement required.

**⚠️ Do NOT re-run Step 1 expecting a reset.** The cutover is complete and idempotent — a fresh `terraform apply` on committed config is now a no-op. The runbook `infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md` §"REMEDIATE the existing exposure" Step 1 still *describes* a CHANGEME reset; that path is obsolete for these 20 slots. Re-forcing a send (e.g. bumping `value_wo_version`) **without** supplying the current-values var-file would write `CHANGEME` and break the box — do not do it.

**What REMAINS in this ticket's scope (deliberately NOT done — exposure remediation was scoped out of the structural change):**
- **State-history scrub** — prior S3 tfstate *versions* still embed the pre-migration cleartext values (the old `value` + `ignore_changes=[value]` design persisted them). The current state is clean; the historical versions are not. Scrubbing S3 object-version history remains operator work.
- **Rotation of exposed crown-jewel secrets** — a value that was ever persisted to state must be considered exposed; you cannot un-expose it by scrubbing, only by rotating. This remains operator work and requires the external-system updates the original charter described.

Keeping this ticket **OPEN** for the scrub + rotation. The apply prerequisite is satisfied, so those two can now proceed independently whenever an operator picks them up.

## Operator remediation — apply the value_wo migration, scrub existing cleartext from remote state, and rotate the exposed crown-jewel secrets

This is the PROD-mutation follow-through for the code change landed under
`finedrawn-closed-stud` (eb67-b96c-dcf0-4f86), which migrated every SSM SecureString
**secret** parameter to terraform write-only arguments (`value_wo` / `value_wo_version`)
so secret values are never persisted to terraform state (ADR 0105). The code change alone
does NOT mutate prod; this ticket is the operator cutover.

**Run this only AFTER the value_wo code change has landed on main.** Follow the procedure in
`infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md` §"REMEDIATE the existing exposure".

### Steps
1. `terraform apply` the value_wo migration. NOTE the one-time cutover reset: on this apply
   `value_wo_version` goes absent -> 1 for each migrated slot, so the provider re-sends
   `value_wo = "CHANGEME"` once and RESETS each live seeded secret to the placeholder. This is
   intended (we rotate these secrets in the same window). `user_data.sh`'s CHANGEME fail-fast is
   the safety net.
2. In the SAME maintenance window, re-seed/ROTATE every affected secret out-of-band
   (`aws ssm put-parameter --overwrite`). Rotate the crown-jewels explicitly — they were exposed
   in cleartext in state and must be treated as compromised: Gerrit admin password, opcert
   Ed25519 signing key, rebar-bot signing key, Anthropic API key, jira-api-token, SSH host keys.
   Update every external system that trusts an old value (Gerrit account, Jira token, bot public
   key, Anthropic console).
3. VERIFY no SecureString value appears in state: `terraform state pull` must show `value: null`
   (and no `value_wo`) for every migrated secret. Only the generated `opcert_origin_guard`
   legitimately still resolves (via its random_password).
4. SCRUB the historical cleartext from the state backend: the prior values persist in the retained
   versions of `s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071/rebar/prod/terraform.tfstate` (bucket versioning,
   ~149 versions). Permanently delete the affected object versions (or roll the bucket / lifecycle-
   expire old versions per data-handling policy). Rotated values are retired but still purge them.

### Coordination
- Coordinate with the SEPARATE "rubied" apply that is seeding 4 new MCP-PAT SSM params so the
  state scrub covers those params too (they are also SecureString secrets under /rebar/prod/).
- Cross-reference: ADR 0105 (docs/adr/0105-ssm-secrets-never-in-terraform-state.md) and the runbook
  infra/runbooks/ssm-secret-write-only.md.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] value_wo migration applied to prod.
- [ ] Every migrated secret re-seeded/rotated; crown-jewels rotated and external trust updated.
- [ ] `terraform state pull` shows no SecureString secret value (all `value: null`, no `value_wo`).
- [ ] Historical cleartext purged from the state bucket's retained versions.
- [ ] rubied MCP-PAT params covered by the same scrub.

## Verification
- Before any state surgery, confirm S3 versioning on `s3://rebar-tfstate-896586841071` and write a names-only SSM parameter snapshot to a local project/session artifact, never values.
- `terraform plan` in `infra/terraform` must show no destructive changes outside the approved value_wo/state-scrub/rotation scope before any apply.
- After the apply/rotation, verify `terraform state pull` has no cleartext SecureString values (`value: null`, no `value_wo` material) without printing secret values.
- Verify every rotated self-regenerable secret's consumers have restarted or re-read the parameter and health checks pass.
- Verify historical cleartext tfstate object versions were removed or retired per the runbook, recording only object/version identifiers and secret names as needed.


## Completion Scope Adjustment (2026-09-07)
The operator's 2026-09-06 approval narrowed autonomous rotation: rotate ONLY secrets that can be regenerated internally in this session, and flag third-party or externally anchored credentials for a human/operator who can reissue the external trust. The executable close scope for this ticket is therefore: value_wo already applied, live/current tfstate and retained historical tfstate versions scrubbed of non-generated SecureString values, and internally self-contained secrets rotated. Externally anchored secrets are tracked in follow-up `auspicial-wily-warbler`, linked `discovered_from`, and are intentionally not blockers for this ticket's close under the narrowed operator instruction.
